sources.title: Exact repository min-subarray-partition question and boundary audit

claims.text: The source asks for the minimum number of subarrays with sums <= k but does not preserve non-negativity, explicit bounds, impossible-return shape, or a clarification of contiguous versus arbitrary grouping.
Under the explicitly stated contiguous full-partition contract with signed int elements, prefix-sum DP over the last cut handles negative values and returns the minimum legal segment count or -1.
The executable fixture covers empty/basic cases, signed rescue, impossible singleton, whole signed segment, exact-k boundaries and long accumulation.

Independent source-first review found no hard failures, unsupported claims or uncovered source variants and recompiled the exact candidate Java against an exhaustive small signed-array cut-mask oracle.

findings: The preserved source asks only for the minimum number of subarrays whose sums are <= k; it does not preserve non-negativity, explicit bounds, empty/impossible return conventions, or an explicit clarification of contiguous versus arbitrary grouping.

The candidate makes those missing pieces explicit as answer-side execution policy rather than recovered source: full ordered partition into non-empty contiguous segments, signed int values, empty -> 0 and impossible -> -1.
Because signed values are allowed by the chosen conservative policy, the prefix-sum last-cut DP is appropriate and does not rely on the monotonicity needed by the usual non-negative greedy shortcut.

The exact Java fence independently compiles on JDK 21 and matches a separate brute-force cut-mask oracle for every array of lengths 1..6 over values -3..3 and k values -4..6, plus empty/extreme-int cases, with no input mutation.
The answer scopes the O(n) greedy optimization only to a later non-negative constraint and does not fabricate project experience or source constraints.
